catalog.name: Waste heat recovery
catalog.description:
As part of the energy transition towards full decarbonization, the use of waste heat and the integration of renewables represent the only two sources of generation for efficient district heating by 2050. Furthermore, heat recovery represents a significant opportunity to increase the efficiency of the industrial sector.

This collection contains maps useful for assessing the potential heat that can be recovered from industrial waste heat and distributed to domestic and tertiary sector users via district heating networks. For this purpose, the following are available:

  • Italian maps of possible industrial heat waste estimated from the data available from industries registered in the ETS register (Emission Trading System), representing energy-intensive industrial sectors (e.g., oil refineries, steel mills, and large-scale production of iron, metals, aluminum, cement, lime, glass, ceramics, pulp and paper, acids, and organic chemicals). These include generating sites already serving district heating networks. The maps are categorized by different waste heat temperature ranges.

  • Maps estimating the heating demand for the residential and tertiary sectors by census area for 2030 based on 2011 ISTAT data.

  • The map estimating recoverable heat and its cost, including distribution, obtained by matching thermal supply and demand with a view to economic sustainability compared to individual heating systems.

The maps are the result of processing carried out jointly by RSE and the Energy Department of the Milan Polytechnic (RELAB - Energy Department).

members.name: High Temperature Waste Heat Estimate - T > 300°C (MWh)
members.description:
Map of the estimated high-temperature waste heat (HT - T> 300°C) calculated for Italian industries registered in the ETS register (Union Registry Public Website). The estimated thermal waste is mapped and themed based on the quantity of waste heat calculated from the CO2 emission data and some recovery coefficients taken from the literature, linked to the type of industry and the temperature level of the effluents. The reported value refers to the energy available for the heating season (6 months).

By clicking on the point you can get additional information such as the estimated amount of waste heat available (MWh), the municipality, etc.

The maps are the result of elaborations carried out jointly by RSE and the Energy Department of the Polytechnic University of Milan (RELAB - Department of Energy) starting from the data of the ETS register (Union Registry Public Website) .

For further details see the System Research reports XXX (DA LINKARE QUANDO SARA' PUBBLICATO), 23012308, 20010734, 21010223.

members.name: Calore di scarto COPERTURA PARZIALE
members.description:
L'atlante italiano del calore di scarto riporta il calore di scarto disponibile per le industrie iscritte al registro ETS comprendente settori industriali ad alta intensità energetica, come raffinerie di petrolio, acciaierie e produzione di ferro, metalli, alluminio, cemento, calce, vetro, ceramica, pasta di legno, carta, acidi e prodotti chimici organici su larga scala. Il calore di scarto disponibile è stato calcolato partendo da una valutazione dell'energia annua consumata utilizzando dei coefficienti percentuali di calore di scarto prodotto riportati in letteratura, legati alla tipologia di industria e temperatura del calore di scarto.

Le mappe sono categorizzate in base alla temperatura del calore e suo utilizzo:

  • Calore di scarto ad Alta Temperatura (HT): T> 300°C
  • Calore di scarto a Media Temperatura (MT): 80
  • Calore di scarto a Bassa Temperatura (LT): T<80°C
  • Impianti di Teleriscaldamento

members.name: Estimated heat demand for heating and domestic hot water in 2030 (MWh/year)
members.description:
Map of the estimated annual heat demand for heating and domestic hot water expected for 2030 by ISTAT census area (data relating to Istat Population and Housing Census 2011).

The estimate of the current heating demand of the residential sector is calculated from known consumption data (from the EUROSTAT National Energy Balance), aggregated on a regional basis (according to the procedure described by GSE in the report "Evaluation of the national and regional potential for the application of high-efficiency cogeneration and efficient district heating") and redistributed across the territory with respect to each census section, considering the characteristics of the buildings (i.e., construction period and surface area) available from the Census, with distinctions for space heating and domestic hot water.

The estimate of the heating demand of the residential sector for 2030 is calculated starting from the current demand data determined in each census section, considering an overall average deep retrofit rate in Italy of 0.7% per year for the residential sector and 2.5% per year for the tertiary sector (consistent with the indications of the PNIEC) and a light retrofit rate for the residential sector of approximately 0.3% per year.

The maps are the result of elaborations carried out jointly by RSE and the Energy Department of the Polytechnic University of Milan (RELAB - Energy Department) starting from regional consumption data and data relating to the sections of the Istat 2011 Population and Housing Census, based on algorithms reported in the document 'Innovative solutions for the energy transition and efficiency of district heating' and in the document 'Evaluation of the potential for the diffusion of efficient district heating across the national territory'.

members.name: Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) of RECOVERABLE HEAT FOR DISTRICT HEATING (€/MWh)
members.description:
The estimate of heat distributed to the network is the result of an optimized matching between the technically district heating demand located within 10 km of the heat source and the economically viable waste heat supply, with a view to competing with domestic heating.

The LCOE takes into account the cost of recovery technology (high- and medium-temperature (HT and MT) heat exchangers and low-temperature (LT) heat pumps) and the cost of the transmission and distribution network. Many industrial heat sources have both high and low temperature heat so the LCOE takes into account the use of both heat inputs.

By clicking on each site with available waste heat, the network connecting the heat source to the center of the served census area is displayed, along the best road routes. The census areas served by the waste heat are also displayed, and finally, the values ​​used and calculated by the optimization software can be consulted

  • distance from the heat source within which the user to be considered is located (radius in m)
  • length of the transport network (m)
  • cost of the transport network (keuro)
  • length of the distribution network (m)
  • cost of the distribution network (k€)
  • waste heat available at HT and MT (MWh)
  • heat supplied to the user recovered from waste heat at HT and MT (MWh)
  • investment cost of recovery technology for HT and MT (k€)
  • waste heat available at LT (MWh)
  • heat supplied to the user recovered from waste heat at LT (MWh)
  • investment cost of waste heat recovery technology per LT (k€)
  • energy served by individual boiler solutions [MWh/year] pertaining to the census areas served by waste heat
  • LCOE - levelized cost of energy of heat distributed to users (€/MWh)

A module can be activated that allows the user to set site-specific data (e.g., the amount of waste heat to consider, the radius within which to consider thermal users, the cost of waste heat, and the energy costs of the individual solution) to ensure a more accurate assessment of the cost of using waste heat for district heating applications. The results of the new optimization are sent to each user via email and can be uploaded to the website.

The maps are the result of processing carried out jointly by RSE and the Energy Department of the Milan Polytechnic (RELAB - Energy Department ).

members.name: Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) del CALORE RECUPERABILE PER TELERISCALDAMENTO (€/MWh)
members.description:
Mappa dei potenziali progetti di recupero del calore di scarto industriale tramite nuove reti di teleriscaldamento e stima del LCOE (Levelized Cost Of Energy €/MWh) del calore di scarto distribuito alle utenze residenziali e terziarie.

La stima del calore distribuito in rete è frutto del matching ottimizzato tra la domanda termica tecnicamente teleriscaldabile situata ad una distanza inferiore a 10 km della fonte di calore, e l'offerta termica di calore di scarto economicamente in un'ottica di competizione con il riscaldamento domestico.

Il LCOE tiene conto del costo della tecnologia di recupero (scambiatore per calore ad alta e media temperatura (HT e MT) e pompe di calore per calore a bassa temperatura (LT)) e del costo della rete di trasmissione e di distribuzione. Molte fonti di calore industriale dispongono sia di calore ad alta che a bassa temperatura per cui il LCOE tiene conto dell'utilizzo di entrambi i contributi di calore.

Cliccando su ciascun sito con calore di scarto disponibile, viene visualizzata la rete che unisce la fonte del calore con il centro dell'area di censimento servita, lungo i migliori percorsi stradali. Vengono inoltre visualizzate le aree di censimento servite dal calore di scarto ed infine sono consultabili i valori utilizzati e calcolati dal software di ottimizzazione

  • distanza della fonte di calore entro cui è situata l’utenza da considerare (raggio in m)
  • lunghezza della rete di trasporto (m)
  • costo della rete di trasporto (keuro)
  • lunghezza della rete di distribuzione (m)
  • costo della rete di distribuzione (k€)
  • calore di scarto disponibile a HT e MT (MWh)
  • calore fornito all'utenza recuperato dal calore di scarto a HT e MT (MWh)
  • costo di investimento della tecnologia di recupero per HT e MT (k€)
  • calore di scarto disponibile a LT (MWh)
  • calore fornito all'utenza recuperato dal calore di scarto a LT (MWh)
  • costo di investimento della tecnologia di recupero per LT (k€)
  • energia servita da soluzioni individuali- boiler [MWh/anno] afferenti alle aree di censimento servite dal calore di scarto
  • LCOE- levelized cost of Energy del calore distribuito all'utenza (€/MWh)

E' possibile attivare un modulo che permette all'utente di impostare alcuni dati sito-specifici (es. quantità di calore di scarto da considerare, il raggio entro cui considerare le utenze termiche, il costo del calore di scarto, i costi dell'energia della soluzione individuale) per garantire una valutazione più accurata del costo dello sfruttamento del calore di scarto per applicazioni di teleriscaldamento. I risultati della nuova ottimizzazione vengono inviati a ciascun utente via mail e possono essere caricati nel sito.

Le mappe sono il risultato di elaborazioni svolte congiuntamente da RSE e dal dipartimento di Energia del Politecnico di Milano (RELAB - Dipartimento di Energia).
